title: Filling a prime grid from its row and column products
description: A three by three grid has row products one hundred and five, twenty and thirty, and column products twenty eight, one hundred and twenty five and eighteen. The video fills the nine cells with primes, and Keeko's doubt that a four can sit in the grid is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: start from the product that allows only one choice, then let each filled cell fix the next one. Watch for students who put a composite number such as four in a cell because it multiplies to the row product.

source: Fill the 3 by 3 grid with prime numbers only so that the product of each row is the number to the right of the row and the product of each column is the number below the column. Row products: 105, 20, 30. Column products: 28, 125, 18.
video_script.why: The child breaks each product into primes, starts with the column that has only one choice, and lets every filled cell fix the next one.
video_script.substitution: Break each product into primes, start with the product made of one prime, then fill the rest cell by cell.
video_script.anchor: an empty 3 by 3 grid with 105, 20 and 30 at the right of the rows and 28, 125 and 18 below the columns
video_script.wrong_answer: the second row can have a four in it
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the second row can have a four in it, because four times five is twenty. Four is two times two, so it is not a prime, and the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: The rows are seven, five, three, then two, five, two, then two, five, three

final_answer.spoken: the rows are seven, five, three, then two, five, two, then two, five, three

never_show: the second row can have a four in it
maths_rules: 125 = 5 x 5 x 5, so the middle column is 5, 5, 5
105 = 3 x 5 x 7 and the middle cell is 5, so the other two cells of the top row are 3 and 7
28 = 2 x 2 x 7 has no 3, so the top-left cell is 7 and the top-right cell is 3
20 = 2 x 2 x 5 and the middle cell is 5, so the second row is 2, 5, 2
the first column is 7 x 2 x 2 = 28, so the bottom-left cell is 2
18 = 2 x 3 x 3 and the right column has 3 and 2, so the bottom-right cell is 3
4 = 2 x 2 is not a prime, so a 4 cannot sit in the grid
video_script.design: One idea: begin with the product that has only one choice and let each filled cell fix the next. Assumes the rules of the puzzle and prime factors. Wrong idea: a composite number can sit in a cell. The grid stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the second row can have a four in it.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Four times five is twenty, which is the number beside that row.
<bookmark mark='twos'/>But four is two times two, so it is not a prime.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Every cell must be a prime, so the four breaks into two twos.
